repo.description:
## Impact

OpenBao's plugin registration APIs (`/v1/sys/plugins/catalog/*`) did not enforce that requests to update registrations can only be made from the root namespace, leading to sufficiently privileged tokens having control over the plugin registrations via the `sys/` mount of a child namespace.

Note that plugin registrations only lead to plugin execution if:

- The `command` parameter of the registration is a valid file name within the host's plugin directory, if one is configured.
- The `sha256sum` parameter of the registration matches the SHA-256 digest of the contents of the file on disk.

This limits the options of an attacker that does not control the host's plugin directory to DoS-like scenarios, such as removing existing registrations, creating entirely invalid ones or creating new ones for installed plugins.

## Patch

This vulnerability is patched in OpenBao v2.7.0 and v2.6.3.

## Workarounds

- Ensure that tenants that should not control the plugin catalog are not granted `write` or `delete` capabilities on `sys/plugins/catalog/*` within their namespace(s).
- Alternatively, disable external plugins entirely by not configuring a `plugin_directory`.

## References

- https://openbao.org/docs/api/system/plugins-catalog

## Reporters

This vulnerability was first reported by @satoqz and later re-reported independently by @MarcIlunga and @opensec-intelligence before publication of the initial report.
repo.summary: OpenBao's Plugin Registration APIs Are Not Limited to the Root Namespace
